--- title: "Fit two runs of real FIAC data" subtitle: "Carry a published 2 x 2 design through the public first-level seam and back to a brain map." jupyter: python3 execute: freeze: auto cache: true --- This tutorial fits two real functional runs from the Functional Imaging Analysis Contest (FIAC). The question is a 2 x 2 factorial one: does the BOLD response differ when a sentence is repeated, and does it differ when the speaker is repeated? We will inspect the inputs, put both runs in one dataset, fit one model, and return the sentence-effect statistic to image space. ::: {.callout-note} ## Before you run it From a source checkout, the `docs` extra installs `nilearn>=0.12` and the current [`neuroim-python`](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/neuroim-python) directly from GitHub. On first use, `fetch_fiac_first_level()` downloads roughly 80 MB and stores it in Nilearn's data cache (by default, `~/nilearn_data`); the process therefore needs network access and a writable cache. Later runs reuse those files. Allow under a minute for a cached run on a typical laptop, with additional time for the first download. The exact timing recorded by the parity workflow appears near the end of this page. Nilearn's packaged dataset description reports the FIAC license as unknown, so confirm the source terms before redistributing the downloaded files. The fetcher supplies functional NIfTI images, a mask, and already-realized design matrices. This is a first-level modeling tutorial, not a preprocessing pipeline: motion correction, distortion correction, registration, and normalization are upstream of fmrimod and out of scope here. ::: ::: {.callout-tip} ## Result and receipt at a glance The public seam below fits both 191-volume runs across all 28,008 in-mask voxels as one `FmriDataset` and one `FmriLm`. `neuroim` owns image reading, 6 mm FWHM smoothing, masking, spatial metadata, and the reconstructed statistic shown on the [landing page](../index.qmd). fmrimod's default `RunwiseEngine` keeps run-specific solves internal to that one model. This remains an interoperability result: Nilearn supplies the download and already-realized design matrices; fmrimod and neuroim own the modeling path from images onward. Native design authoring is taught separately. A narrower checked-in receipt near the end verifies fmrimod's explicit Nilearn-compatible equal-weight pooling route; it is clearly separated from the default multi-run map shown here. ::: ## Fetch and inspect the inputs ::: {#d987e0b1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from pathlib import Path import numpy as np import pandas as pd import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import neuroim as ni from nilearn.datasets import fetch_fiac_first_level from nilearn.plotting import plot_design_matrix import fmrimod as fm from fmrimod.design import RealizedDesign from fmrimod.model.config import FmriLmConfig fiac = fetch_fiac_first_level(verbose=0) run_paths = (Path(fiac.func1), Path(fiac.func2)) run_vecs = tuple(ni.read_vec(path) for path in run_paths) design_matrices = ( fiac.design_matrix1.copy(), fiac.design_matrix2.copy(), ) mask_vol = ni.read_vol(fiac.mask) tr = float(np.diff(design_matrices[0].index.to_numpy()[:2])[0]) ``` ::: Each `NeuroVec` contains 191 whole-brain volumes. The `NeuroVol` mask defines the features that enter the model. Both retain the spatial transform needed to return a result to the same brain grid. ::: {#64c0970a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} input_summary = pd.DataFrame( { "run": (1, 2), "file": tuple(path.name for path in run_paths), "image shape (x, y, z, time)": tuple( str(tuple(int(value) for value in vec.space.dim)) for vec in run_vecs ), "design shape": tuple(str(dm.shape) for dm in design_matrices), "TR (s)": tr, "in-mask voxels": int(np.count_nonzero(mask_vol.data)), } ) input_summary ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
run file image shape (x, y, z, time) design shape TR (s) in-mask voxels
0 1 run1.nii.gz (64, 64, 30, 191) (191, 13) 1.0 28008
1 2 run2.nii.gz (64, 64, 30, 191) (191, 13) 1.0 28008
``` ::: ::: The four factorial cells encode **Sentence** (same, `SSt`, or different, `DSt`) crossed with **Speaker** (same, `SSp`, or different, `DSp`). `FirstSt` pools the first sentence across conditions; the drift columns model slow variation. These are the actual columns used in both runs, not names reconstructed for the tutorial. ::: {#9f7911d6 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} pd.DataFrame( { "column": design_matrices[0].columns, "role": [ "factorial cell" if i < 4 else "nuisance" for i in range(design_matrices[0].shape[1]) ], } ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
column role
0 SSt-SSp factorial cell
1 SSt-DSp factorial cell
2 DSt-SSp factorial cell
3 DSt-DSp factorial cell
4 FirstSt nuisance
5 drift:0 nuisance
6 drift:1 nuisance
7 drift:2 nuisance
8 drift:3 nuisance
9 drift:4 nuisance
10 drift:5 nuisance
11 drift:6 nuisance
12 drift:7 nuisance
``` ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-fiac-design .cell fig-height='4.8' fig-width='9' execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} design_ax = plot_design_matrix(design_matrices[0]) plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![The realized design supplied with FIAC run 1. The first four columns are the 2 x 2 experimental cells; the remaining columns model the pooled first sentence and low-frequency drift.](real-data-fiac_files/figure-html/fig-fiac-design-output-1.png){#fig-fiac-design fig-alt='FIAC run-one design matrix with 191 time points in rows and thirteen labeled columns. The first four columns are the Sentence by Speaker factorial cells, followed by FirstSt and eight smooth drift terms.'} ::: ::: ## Fit one multi-run model through the public seam The public dataset owns both runs. `neuroim` performs the image operations and fmrimod's adapter performs the masked image-to-matrix boundary internally: ```text NeuroVec[2] -> fmri_dataset -> RealizedDesign(source="nilearn") -> fmri_lm ``` Because the imported run designs share the same columns, their rows can be stacked in acquisition order. `RealizedDesign` carries that matrix, its stable column names, and its source. The Moore-Penrose solver is selected explicitly for this externally realized design. The engine still estimates each run separately because run boundaries carry statistical meaning. That split is engine work, not user orchestration: the user passes one dataset and receives one fit. ::: {#5b7b40a1 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} smoothing_fwhm_mm = 6.0 analysis_vecs = tuple( ni.gaussian_blur(vec, fwhm_mm=smoothing_fwhm_mm) for vec in run_vecs ) dataset = fm.fmri_dataset( analysis_vecs, mask=mask_vol, tr=tr, slice_timing_offset=0.0, ) design_columns = tuple(str(column) for column in design_matrices[0].columns) assert all( tuple(str(column) for column in design.columns) == design_columns for design in design_matrices ) realized_design = RealizedDesign.from_array( np.vstack( [design.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64) for design in design_matrices] ), columns=design_columns, source="nilearn", ) fit = fm.fmri_lm( realized_design, dataset, config=FmriLmConfig(solver="pinv"), ) assert fit.provenance.design_source == "nilearn" assert len(fit.run_results) == dataset.n_runs pd.DataFrame( { "runs in dataset": [dataset.n_runs], "run lengths": [str(dataset.run_lengths)], "in-mask voxels": [fit.n_voxels], "design rows": [realized_design.n_timepoints], "design source": [fit.provenance.design_source], "engine": [fit.provenance.solver_path], } ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
runs in dataset run lengths in-mask voxels design rows design source engine
0 2 [191, 191] 28008 382 nilearn RunwiseEngine
``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-important} ## What this path does—and does not—prove This is an **interop bridge**. It proves that neuroim-backed images and an externally realized design can enter one typed multi-run dataset/model, retain `source="nilearn"` provenance, and produce public fit, contrast, and NeuroVol objects. It does **not** prove native fmrimod design authoring for FIAC, because Nilearn supplied the matrix before fmrimod saw it. Carrying a matrix safely is not the same claim as expressing the experiment as an fmrimod event-design specification. ::: ## State the two main effects by column meaning The sentence main effect is the mean of both same-sentence cells minus the mean of both different-sentence cells. The speaker main effect makes the corresponding comparison across speaker levels. The patterns below name those sets of imported columns; fmrimod resolves and normalizes their weights. No positional vector is constructed or passed to `contrast()`. ::: {#474dfa43 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} main_effects = { "sentence_effect": fm.column_contrast( pattern_A=r"^SSt-", pattern_B=r"^DSt-", name="sentence_effect", ), "speaker_effect": fm.column_contrast( pattern_A=r"-SSp$", pattern_B=r"-DSp$", name="speaker_effect", ), } results = { name: fit.contrast(spec) for name, spec in main_effects.items() } pd.DataFrame( [ { "contrast": name, "statistic": result.stat_type, "residual df": result.df, "min t": result.stat.min(), "max t": result.stat.max(), } for name, result in results.items() ] ).round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
contrast statistic residual df min t max t
0 sentence_effect t 356.0 -6.13 5.928
1 speaker_effect t 356.0 -6.19 4.707
``` ::: ::: These patterns are safer than weights tied to column positions, but they still depend on the names in the imported matrix. A natively authored factorial design would let the hypothesis refer directly to declared factor levels; this tutorial does not claim that stronger interface. ## Return the sentence statistic to the brain `results["sentence_effect"].stat` is one value per masked voxel. `to_neurovol()` uses the spatial context retained by the dataset to restore those values to the FIAC grid—no masker or hand-written reshape is needed. A 6 mm FWHM Gaussian smooth is applied to each BOLD run before fitting. For these 3 x 3 x 4 mm voxels, that produces a more legible descriptive map than the earlier 4 mm display while remaining within a conventional single-subject scale. The display threshold of `|t| >= 2` is descriptive; it is not corrected for multiple comparisons. ::: {#e77ba6dc .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} sentence_t_vol = results["sentence_effect"].to_neurovol("stat") background_vol = ni.concat(*analysis_vecs).mean() ``` ::: ::: {#cell-fig-fiac-sentence-effect .cell fig-height='6' fig-width='11' execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} display_threshold = 2.0 display_limit = 5.0 slice_indices = (8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22) montage_fig, montage_axes = ni.plot_overlay( background=background_vol, overlay=sentence_t_vol, zlevels=slice_indices, axis="z", ncol=4, figsize=(11, 5.8), threshold=display_threshold, overlay_cmap="blue-red", ov_range=(-display_limit, display_limit), ov_cap=display_limit, alpha=0.92, colorbar=True, crop=0.06, title="Sentence effect: same − different", ) for axis, slice_index in zip(montage_axes, slice_indices): z_coord = float( sentence_t_vol.space.grid_to_coord([[0, 0, slice_index]])[0, 2] ) axis.set_title(f"z = {z_coord:.0f} mm", fontsize=10, pad=5, color="#252a34") axis.text( 0.02, 0.88, "L", transform=axis.transAxes, fontsize=9, color="white" ) axis.text( 0.98, 0.88, "R", transform=axis.transAxes, fontsize=9, color="white", ha="right", ) montage_fig.axes[-1].set_ylabel("t statistic", fontsize=10) docs_root = next( candidate for candidate in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents) if (candidate / "_quarto.yml").is_file() ) montage_fig.savefig( docs_root / "assets/fiac-sentence-effect.png", dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight", facecolor="white", ) plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Sentence statistic (same sentence minus different sentence) from one neuroim-backed, two-run fmrimod model. The BOLD data were smoothed at 6 mm FWHM before fitting; colors show absolute t statistics of at least 2 for spatial orientation, not corrected inference.](real-data-fiac_files/figure-html/fig-fiac-sentence-effect-output-1.png){#fig-fiac-sentence-effect fig-alt='A centered two-by-four montage of axial FIAC brain slices from z equals 32 through 88 millimeters. On the participant\'s mean functional image, red areas show positive same-sentence minus different-sentence t statistics of at least 2 and blue areas show negative values of at most minus 2.'} ::: ::: The result is a `neuroim.DenseNeuroVol` in the source geometry. It can be converted to a nibabel image with `.to_nibabel()` or written as NIfTI, but the analysis and figure do not need to leave the neuroim data model. ## Read the adjacent parity receipt The figure shows that the workflow produces an interpretable image; it does not establish agreement with an independent implementation. The checked-in FIAC receipt asks a narrower cross-implementation question: when fmrimod uses explicit per-run fits plus `combine_runs()` for Nilearn-compatible equal-weight fixed pooling, do these same sentence and speaker estimands agree with Nilearn? Its gate uses a deterministic 2,048-voxel subset of the same mask to keep repeated parity runs inexpensive. That receipt reports on the explicit equal-weight pooling path, not on the default `RunwiseEngine` map above. Keeping the two claims separate avoids presenting a neighboring parity result as evidence for a different estimator. ::: {#9a6770c2 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} import json repo_root = next( candidate for candidate in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents) if (candidate / "benchmarks/parity/tier_a_fiac").is_dir() ) receipt_path = ( repo_root / "benchmarks/parity/tier_a_fiac/reports/parity_report.json" ) receipt = json.loads(receipt_path.read_text()) assert receipt["name"] == "tier_a_fiac_fixed_effects" print(f"status: {receipt['status']}") print(f"caveats: {receipt['caveats'] or 'none'}") print(f"recorded parity-workflow runtime: {receipt['timings']['seconds']:.3f} s") pd.DataFrame( [ { "quantity": name, "max |fmrimod - Nilearn|": delta["max_abs"], "mean absolute error": delta["mae"], "gate": delta["gate"], "pass": delta["passes"], } for name, delta in receipt["deltas"].items() ] ).sort_values("quantity") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` status: pass caveats: none recorded parity-workflow runtime: 2.419 s ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: The receipt is generated by the executable workflow in `benchmarks/parity/tier_a_fiac/workflow.py`; it is not copied from another benchmark. From a source checkout, regenerate it with: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m benchmarks.parity.tier_a_fiac.workflow ``` ## Where to go next You can now carry two model-ready NIfTI runs through one neuroim-backed fmrimod dataset and fit, then recover a typed statistical volume without losing design provenance or hand-aligning contrast weights. - [Build design matrices](design-matrices.qmd) to author a design from events inside fmrimod rather than importing a realized matrix. - [Contrasts](contrasts.qmd) to use semantic condition-level hypotheses when the design was authored natively. - [Group analysis](group-analysis.qmd) to carry first-level contrasts into a second-level model.
